title: Aurum PropTech Ltd - 539289 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Aurum PropTech Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 70.9% YoY to INR 111.84 crore and PBT turned positive at INR 2.31 crore, with Housing.com acquisition announced.
summary.overview: Aurum PropTech reported its third consecutive profitable quarter, with revenue from operations of INR 111.84 crore (up 70.9% YoY but down from INR 123.85 crore QoQ) and PBT of INR 2.31 crore (2.1% margin). Management said PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins 1,320 bps YoY. The quarter also featured the announced acquisition of Housing.com, which management says is loss-making and targeted to reach profitability in four to six quarters; the company guided to a burn of about INR 200 crore annualised at Housing. Management also said the INR 112 crore sale of a building closed during the quarter, contributing INR 52.38 crore of other income from discontinued operations.

segments.name: Rental
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 54.35 crore with 81% occupancy across 21 cities (student housing, co-living, family rentals); segment profit INR 0.63 crore. Management says both rental businesses reached adjusted EBITDA profitability.

segments.name: Distribution (developer and distribution)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 55.94 crore, down from INR 66.87 crore QoQ; segment profit INR 7.97 crore. Platform serves over 1,200 developers across 1,50,000 projects in 40+ cities.

segments.name: Capital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.55 crore, down from INR 4.28 crore QoQ; segment loss of INR 0.05 crore.

segments.name: Discontinued operations (building sale)
segments.commentary: Building sold for INR 112 crore; other income from discontinued operations INR 52.38 crore in the quarter (INR 17.78 crore in previous quarter). Discontinued-operations PBT INR 52.40 crore.

guidance_outlook: Housing.com to reach adjusted profitability (break-even) in four to six quarters publicly; internal target three to four quarters.
Management expects Housing.com burn of about INR 200 crore annualised as-is; cost streamlining targeted post-closing.
Company-level profitability possible within two to three quarters per management response; formal guidance deferred until Housing deal closes.
Tax and financial-metric long-term positions for Housing to be articulated in Q3 FY27 (starting H2).
Management says INR 1,000 crore ARR target expected to be reached faster with Housing.com; no numerical guidance given.
Promoters to subscribe to equity; INR 200 odd crore war chest for Housing; combined REA stake to rise to around 24.9% after Housing swap (REA already ~5% from PropTiger).
capex_capacity: Housing.com acquisition is being structured by swapping shares with REA Group, which will take about 20% additional equity; closing pending.
Housing.com FY26 financials under audit; July-June calendar; to be disclosed in coming quarters.
Rental portfolio spans 21 cities with focus on occupancy (81%) rather than inventory expansion.
Sell.do: over 1,000 developers onboarded and 11,800+ active licences; FY26 gross churn 7%.
demand_pricing: Housing.com holds about 24% of India's online portal market; online portals capture about INR 1,200 crore of an estimated INR 38,000 crore annual property marketing and mortgage spend (less than 5% penetration).
Housing.com has 58 million average monthly visits and 12 million monthly active users on the app.
Housing.com FY25 revenue from operations about INR 343 crore; FY25 expenses about INR 531 crore (employee, other expenses incl. advertising, payment gateways, software data).
PropTiger brokerage is slab-based on annual gross transaction targets with developers; Q1 seasonally lower as slabs unlock in second half of the year.
Management cited marketplaces valued at 4.5x revenue in India and 10x in another marketplace; says Aurum acquired Housing at about 1.5x revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation risk between Housing.com organic listings and Aurum Analytica paid lead generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no cannibalisation and views Housing as adding an end-to-end vertical from listings to advertising, lead generation and transactions.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Housing.com market share go over the next two to three years and what tax rate should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to upsell more SKUs within the Housing cohort and extend into transactions; tax structure evaluation is ongoing, with positions to be given in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and loss at Housing.com and what are the priority fixes?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: monetise intent via transactions, increase utilisation of under-used Housing SKUs, ancillary cross-selling, cut top-heavy corporate costs, streamline sales team and marketing spend (Meta, Google). Target four to six quarters to break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What is Housing.com's FY26 loss and burn, and how does it compare with 99acres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Housing's current burn is about INR 200 crore annualised; FY26 numbers still under audit and to be shared later. It argued listing-only models carry losses and the transaction layer is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: How will dilution and ecosystem cross-selling be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Deora said the REA stake (24.9% post-deal) brings strategic value; Housing adds the top of the funnel for cross-selling to PropTiger, KuberX and Analytica. No numerical cross-sell metric was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be profitable at company level within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees potential for company-level profitability as existing businesses are profitable, but will guide after the Housing deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Shrikant Jagtap said a PropTiger revenue category crystallised on target-slab achievement in Q4 FY26; slabs unlock mainly in the second half, so the drop is seasonal rather than one-time.

risks_watch: Housing.com burn of about INR 200 crore annualised; break-even timeline slipped from three to four quarters internally to four to six quarters publicly.
Dilution: REA stake rising to about 24.9% after Housing share swap; INR 200 crore war chest and promoter subscription.
Quarter-on-quarter revenue decline (INR 123.85 crore to INR 111.84 crore) and distribution revenue down to INR 55.94 crore from INR 66.87 crore.
Reported profit in Q1 is heavily supported by INR 52.38 crore discontinued-operations other income; PBT excluding this would be a loss.
Tax-loss runway and effective tax rate not yet disclosed.
Closing of Housing.com acquisition and disclosure of audited FY26 Housing financials.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on the turnaround playbook and Housing synergies, but evasive on hard numbers: Housing's FY26 financials, tax position, multi-year margin guidance and cross-sell metrics were all deferred until after deal closing or later quarters.
key_quotes: Q1 of FY27 is our third consecutive profitable quarter.
Despite Q1 being the industry's softest quarter, our margins improved by 1,000+ basis points.
So now our challenge is not getting 1+1=2 and making that profitable; our challenge really is how to make 1+1=3.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management gives Housing.com breakeven in 4-6 quarters (internal 3-4) with cost streamlining post-closing and no specific capacity or orders, while the quarter's revenue fell QoQ and the 70.9% YoY rise is not backed by a stated forward growth number.
